title: Workspace Purpose
applicability: Introduces the purpose of the 2D state-event procedure design workspace in BestNameYet/Terminals.
purpose: Design and document an MCP-based, interactive two-dimensional State × Event function-pointer procedure machine. Its prototype uses schema-governed agent returns, a context object passed between state functions, and two interactive queue phases for procedure preparation and review/execution, while preserving a complete persisted run record.

title: Machine-Dialect Requirements for Workspace Agent Instructions
applicability: Every current and future entry, including nested instructional members and examples, in workspaces/2d-state-event-procedure-design/AGENTS.json.
required_behavior: Write and interpret every entry in this AGENTS.json according to both the explicit requirements and the spirit of machine dialect: preserve complete intended behavioral meaning, describe scope and required actions unambiguously, and provide enough operational context for an agent to interpret each instruction without guessing. Apply the complete authoritative definition reproduced verbatim below, including all of its writing requirements, contrastive examples, and validation criteria.

title: Mandatory Two-Dimensional State × Event Function-Pointer Architecture
applicability: Governs the design, implementation, extension, validation, execution, queuing, resumption, and testing of every procedure-machine state, event, dispatch table, function pointer, transition handler, and associated context exchange developed in this workspace.

architectural_definition.dimensions: The two independent dispatch dimensions are the current state and the received event type. The function is not a dimension: it is the handler selected by the function pointer located at the intersection of those two dimensions.
architectural_definition.state: A state is a callable operation State_i(e) invoked by the iterator at the current zero-based index i. At entry the state checks e.error, captures any pending diagnostic, selects normal or additive error mode, clears the pending error indicator, and returns a state object with references to externally configurable instruction, schema, and diagnostic content. It never renders the response. The state identifier remains the row key of the two-dimensional State × Event dispatch table.
architectural_definition.event: An event represents a response returned by an agent. In the initial prototype the event type is E_RETURN, with the complete context object e as its payload. The event is agnostic to whether the response is valid or invalid; validity, success, and failure are outcomes assessed by the selected handler, not separate event types.
architectural_definition.function_pointer: The dispatch table is indexed by (current_state, event_type); each populated intersection holds a dedicated validation function pointer. In the initial prototype Dispatch[State_i][E_RETURN] selects Function_i, with i starting at zero. Function_i validates e.e_i and its cross-property constraints, populates e.error on rejection, and returns (e, valid). The iterator, not Function_i, applies the Boolean to i and calls next(e).
architectural_definition.context_object: The complete context object e passes between the iterator, state functions, event handlers and renderer. Independently addressable accepted properties retain their original addresses: State_i requests e.e_i in the indexed prototype. A failed validation may add a diagnostic at e.error. A state captures a pending diagnostic before clearing e.error. Missing required previously accepted context is an implementation error, distinct from an invalid newly submitted property.
architectural_definition.transition: Upon E_RETURN(e), the dispatcher selects Function_i using the current state and event. Function_i independently validates the input and returns (e, true) on acceptance or (e, false) with e.error populated on rejection. The iterator sets i_next = i + Number(valid). True advances exactly one index; false retains i so next(e) rerenders the same state with additive error diagnostic. Neither the event nor agent self-assessment determines validity or destination.
architectural_definition.initialization: The iterator initializes i=0 and e={} unless explicit persisted position and context are provided. It invokes next(e), which calls State_i(e), constructs the state object, and renders it through the separate renderer. The default State_0 argument may supply {} on first entry; retry is initiated by next(e), not a call from Function_0. State functions consume e; no validation-handler-supplied second state argument is required.
architectural_definition.persistence_and_handoff: A procedure preserves the complete accepted context e, current iterator index i, pending diagnostic, and run history across queue handoff, suspension and resumption. The resumed iterator continues at the same position and uses the same State × Event dispatch table; transport does not redefine states, events, validation functions, or Boolean-controlled advancement.

mandatory_behavior.non_deviation: Every state, event, dispatch cell, validation function, iterator step, retry, rendering action, queue handoff and continuation must preserve the State × Event function-pointer architecture and zero-based iterator contract. The only index transition after an agent return is i_next = i + Number(valid). Do not substitute direct state calls inside Function_i, validity-coded event types, agent-selected next states, or a monolithic switch that replaces dispatch.
mandatory_behavior.schema_contracts: Every state must issue a return schema describing the new data expected from the agent, and the tool-response instruction must explain the expected input shape of every non-obvious key, including nested fields and references. The agent returns the complete updated e.
mandatory_behavior.handler_contracts: Each dedicated Function_i validates the agent-return context e independently against its referenced schema and semantic constraints, returns e and an application-determined Boolean valid, and sets e.error on validation failure. It does not invoke a state or alter i. The iterator is responsible for applying the Boolean and invoking next(e).
mandatory_behavior.continuity: Accepted properties of e must remain available under their original independent addresses for later states. Subsequent procedure, simulation, execution, and diagnostic representations must preserve existing change-to-action associations and decorate them rather than independently recreating parallel lists.
mandatory_behavior.prohibited_substitution: Do not reframe the dispatch as a function-by-state table, a validity-by-state table, or a plain linear list that omits State × Event lookup. State and event remain dispatch dimensions, even with one E_RETURN column. The iterator uses the table-selected function's Boolean rather than inventing a separate routing or transition system.

dispatch_notation.invocation: Function_i(e) validates e.e_i and returns (e, valid); the iterator computes i += Number(valid) and calls next(e).
dispatch_notation.interpretation: Rows are state values; columns are event types; cells are callable validation-function pointers. i is zero-based and indexes State_i, Function_i and the requested context property e.e_i.

examples.title: Initialization and accepted first return
sequence: Set i=0 and e={}; next(e) calls State_0(e), which requests e.e0 through externally referenced instruction and JSON schema content.
The renderer displays the normal instruction and schema, and the agent returns E_RETURN(e) containing e.e0.
Dispatch[State_0][E_RETURN] selects Function_0. Function_0 validates e.e0 and returns (e, true).
The iterator increments i from zero to one and calls next(e), which invokes State_1(e).

examples.title: Rejected input stays at the same index
sequence: At index i=2, State_2(e) requests e.e2 and the agent returns E_RETURN(e) containing an invalid e.e2.
Dispatch[State_2][E_RETURN] selects Function_2, which sets e.error={error:true,errortype:'state_2.input_error'} with appropriate reference or structured diagnostic data and returns (e, false).
The iterator leaves i=2 and calls next(e). State_2 captures e.error, selects additive error mode, clears the pending error indicator, and returns the state object.
The renderer displays the error conspicuously before the complete unchanged normal instruction and JSON schema. The event remains E_RETURN, not an INVALID event.

examples.title: Independent context addresses
sequence: After accepted states zero and one, e.e0 retains the original prompt and e.e1 retains the user intent.
State_2(e) reads those prior addresses and requests questions at e.e2.
Function_2 validates e.e2 without reconstructing or overwriting the prior accepted values.

examples.title: Simulation validation
sequence: State_10(e) requests the state-specific simulation input e.e10 while preserving the existing action-to-change mappings.
The agent returns E_RETURN(e); Function_10 is selected at Dispatch[State_10][E_RETURN] and checks the return schema and supported validations.
Function_10 returns (e, true) for acceptance or (e, false) with a diagnostic; only the iterator advances or retries.

examples.title: Queue continuation
sequence: The application persists the entire run context and iterator index for interactive handoff.
A second agent resumes at the carried index, sees the referenced state instruction and schema, and returns E_RETURN(e).
Dispatch[State_i][E_RETURN] selects Function_i; the iterator applies its Boolean and preserves the carried run record.

conformance_test: Conformance requires: zero-based State_i/Function_i/e.e_i correspondence; State × Event dispatch yielding the dedicated Function_i; agent submissions as E_RETURN(e) without validity-coded event types; Function_i returning (e, valid) and setting e.error upon rejection; iterator-only Boolean index update and next(e); additive error rendering with single-use error reset; and preservation of context, index and run across handoffs.

title: State Tool-Response Input Instructions and JSON Return-Schema Alignment
applicability: Every state rendered to an agent through the MCP-based two-dimensional State × Event procedure machine, including initial entry, re-entry after validation errors, queue-resumed interactions, and subsequent procedure phases.

model_definition.state_meaning: State_i(e) denotes a state object generated by an iterator-invoked state function. The state checks e.error before selecting normal or additive error mode, preserves pending diagnostics in the returned object, clears the error indicator, and references externally stored instructions and JSON return schema. The renderer resolves references without deciding mode or progression.
model_definition.expected_input: The expected agent return is the complete context e with existing accepted properties retained and the newly requested e.e_i property populated for current zero-based State_i. In a validation retry the same property e.e_i is requested again.
model_definition.two_required_presentations: Every rendered state presents its expected input in two consistent forms: (1) a complete machine-dialect instruction in sentences and (2) a syntactically valid JSON return schema. Both presentations are authored in addressable external configuration files, selected by references contained in the state object, and assembled by the renderer. Neither is hardcoded as display text inside a script.
model_definition.input_contract_boundary: State invocation and returned-agent-input validation have separate contracts. next(e) invokes State_i(e) at the current index; the state returns a referenced normal or additive error-mode object. The agent returns E_RETURN(e) meeting the current state's schema. Dispatch[State_i][E_RETURN] selects Function_i to validate e.e_i and return (e, valid), after which the iterator changes or retains i. The function does not supply a second argument or directly invoke the destination state.

mandatory_behavior.machine_dialect_statement: For each state, generate a sentence-form instruction applying machine-dialect requirements to identify the input being requested, the values the agent must derive or preserve, their relationships to preceding context e, and any relevant cardinality, identity, ordering, or allowed-value constraints. The statement must be sufficiently complete for an agent to construct the requested return without inferring undocumented meanings.
mandatory_behavior.valid_json_return_schema: In the same rendered tool response, display a real, syntactically valid JSON return schema as JSON, not pseudo-JSON, TypeScript notation, abbreviated field declarations, or an unexplained example payload. The schema must specify the expected object structure, data types, required properties, and applicable structural constraints so the submitted agent return can be validated.
mandatory_behavior.mandatory_sentence_for_every_nontrivial_: For every non-trivial key present anywhere in the JSON return schema, including nested object properties and array-item properties, the machine-dialect instruction statement must include at least one complete sentence explaining that key's intended value and expected input shape. The explanation must state what belongs in the field, not merely repeat the field name or JSON type. For worked examples illustrating complete sentence-form explanations of schema keys, including nested object properties and array-item properties, use the state instruction and return-schema pairs in the referenced workspace file: https://github.com/BestNameYet/Terminals/blob/main/workspaces/2d-state-event-procedure-design/state-instructions-and-return-schemas.json. The referenced examples illustrate this requirement and do not replace the instruction or schema for the current runtime state.
mandatory_behavior.cross_representation_alignment: The machine-dialect statement and the displayed JSON return schema must describe the same expected agent input. Every required field, nested relationship, array size limitation, enumeration, identifier reference, and other significant schema constraint must be represented consistently in the statement; no statement may request a structurally incompatible return and no schema may silently impose an unexplained non-trivial requirement.
mandatory_behavior.full_context_preservation: At State_i the rendered instruction and schema must require e with previously accepted properties retained and e.e_i newly supplied. Error-mode retries request the same property again with the same normal schema and instruction, preceded by the diagnostic.
mandatory_behavior.validation_responsibility: The state-event-selected Function_i validates e.e_i and the documented semantic constraints and returns (e, valid). The iterator updates the index; State_i detects and clears its pending e.error during state-object construction. Missing previously guaranteed context is an implementation error, not automatically a validation error for newly requested input.
mandatory_behavior.nonconformance: A rendered state is nonconforming when it omits either required input presentation, displays invalid JSON as the return schema, leaves a non-trivial schema key without a sentence-form explanation, or gives machine-dialect and schema definitions that disagree. Correct the rendered state contract before treating it as an acceptable procedure-machine state.

examples.title: Conforming State_2 response requesting identified question array at e.e2
examples.rendered_machine_dialect_instruction: Read e.e0 as the previously accepted verbatim user prompt. Read e.e1 as the previously accepted user-intent object; its intent field is a statement of user purpose, objectives is an array of goal strings, constraints is an array of limitation strings, and requested_outcome describes the desired result. Preserve e.e0 and e.e1 unchanged. Add e.e2 as an array containing seven to eleven question objects. In each object, id must be a unique stable question identifier string such as Q1, and question must be a complete question sentence. Return all three properties in e. Function_2 checks identifier uniqueness in addition to JSON Schema validation.
examples.implementation_interpretation: The real JSON schema and the field-by-field prose describe State_2 requesting e.e2. Function_2 performs any additional documented semantic checks and returns a Boolean to the iterator. The state itself does not validate the agent return.

examples.title: Nonconforming unexplained nested key
examples.explanation: This example violates the rule because the sentence does not explain what execution_order means, how the integer relates to other steps, or what the identifiers in action_ids reference. These meanings must be explained in complete sentences alongside the schema.

title: Deterministic Event-Driven State Transitions and Context Argument Passing
applicability: Every transition, agent-submitted event, event/context property, selected function, and state invocation in the interactive two-dimensional State × Event procedure machine, including validation retries and transitions between queue phases.

definitions.ordered_deterministic_route: The procedure follows zero-based indexed states. The current index i is advanced by exactly one when the State × Event-selected Function_i returns true and retained when it returns false. Both outcomes deterministically invoke next(e).
definitions.agent_event: A procedure event is the agent's submission of its response to the current state's tool-response request. In this prototype, the agent returns E_RETURN(e), where e is the complete event/context object; the event type does not classify the input as valid or invalid.
definitions.context_address: A context address is an independently recallable member of e; in the indexed prototype e.e0 holds the verbatim prompt, e.e1 holds user intent, and State_i requests e.e_i. These addresses remain stable when later values accumulate.
definitions.selected_function: At current index i and event type E_RETURN, Dispatch[State_i][E_RETURN] selects Function_i. It validates e.e_i, returns (e, valid), and never directly invokes state functions.
definitions.state_arguments: State_i is invoked by next(e) with the complete context e. A pending validation diagnostic is communicated in e.error rather than a second handler-generated state argument. The state captures the diagnostic before clearing it.

mandatory_behavior.deterministic_transition_order: For any E_RETURN(e) at index i, dispatch Function_i using current State_i and E_RETURN. Apply the returned Boolean by i_next=i+Number(valid). Invoke next(e) at the resulting index. A failed validation retains i and triggers additive error-mode rendering of the same state.
mandatory_behavior.agent_input_drives_events: Treat the agent's response to a rendered state's instruction and JSON return schema as the event input. The agent supplies e; the event does not itself select a transition or encode validation success or failure.
mandatory_behavior.unique_specified_input_addresses: Assign the new input for State_i to e.e_i, with i zero-based, and document its shape in the state instruction and return schema. Preserve earlier accepted e.e0 through e.e_(i-1) under their original addresses.
mandatory_behavior.function_event_argument: Invoke the selected state-event function with e as an argument. The function must inspect or operate on at least one explicitly identified member of e for that event, and may also use other required members for validation or state derivation. If a required member is absent or empty despite the function's input contract requiring it, classify that as an implementation error rather than silently fabricating a value.
mandatory_behavior.function_controls_next_state: Function_i controls the validation outcome but does not directly choose or invoke a destination state. Its true/false return is the sole input to the iterator's prescribed one-step advance or same-state retry; the iterator makes the index transition.
mandatory_behavior.state_receives_derived_arguments: The iterator passes e explicitly to State_i, including any diagnostic at e.error. State_i reads prior accepted values directly from documented e addresses, snapshots the pending error for rendering, and clears e.error. Transition functions must not supply hidden globals or second arguments as an alternative carrier.
mandatory_behavior.initial_invocation_contract: The iterator initializes i=0 and e={} unless resuming an existing run, then calls next(e) to invoke State_0(e). State_0 may accept a default empty e for the initial call. Reentry after rejection occurs through the iterator retaining i and invoking next(e), not through Function_i directly calling a state.

examples.title: Accepted input advances exactly once
sequence: At i=0 the iterator invokes State_0(e), which requests e.e0.
The agent returns E_RETURN(e), and Dispatch[State_0][E_RETURN] invokes Function_0 to validate e.e0.
Function_0 returns (e, true), so the iterator increments i to 1 and invokes next(e), which calls State_1(e).

examples.title: Validation retry does not change event type
sequence: At i=2 the agent returns an invalid e.e2 in E_RETURN(e).
Dispatch[State_2][E_RETURN] selects Function_2; it adds e.error, returns (e,false), and does not invoke a state.
The iterator retains i=2 and invokes next(e); State_2 snapshots and clears the pending error and constructs the error-mode state object.

examples.title: Context is passed through e
sequence: State_3(e) may read accepted e.e0, e.e1 and e.e2 and request e.e3.
Function_3 validates the new e.e3 and returns the full e together with a Boolean.
Both success and retry pass e directly into the iterator's next(e), preserving prior accepted properties.

conformance: Every transition must dispatch the dedicated Function_i by (State_i, E_RETURN); operate on the indexed input e.e_i; return (e, valid); and let only the iterator update i by Number(valid), invoking next(e). Previously accepted context addresses and additive error-mode behavior must remain intact.
implementation_choice_status: The selected implementation is zero-based indexed iterator advancement. Earlier direct state-invocation and deferred next-state-pointer examples are superseded; neither is an implementation alternative to this contract.

title: State-Event Transition Function Invocation and Explicit State Arguments
applicability: Every dispatch of an agent-return event to a transition function, its return-schema validation, and its invocation or return of a destination state in the interactive two-dimensional State × Event function-pointer procedure machine.

architectural_contract.intersection_selection: At iterator index i starting at zero, Dispatch[State_i][E_RETURN] selects Function_i, the dedicated validation function for the input requested by State_i.
architectural_contract.event_consumption: Function_i receives the complete returned context e, validates the newly requested property e.e_i and necessary cross-property constraints, and preserves earlier accepted properties at their original addresses.
architectural_contract.validation: Function_i independently checks the referenced JSON return schema and documented semantics. It returns (e, true) only on acceptance or (e, false) after setting e.error on a validation failure.
architectural_contract.invalid_response_route: A rejection populates e.error with error=true and errortype plus externally resolved diagnostic references or structured diagnostic facts, and returns (e, false). The iterator retains i and invokes next(e). State_i selects error mode, captures and clears the diagnostic, and requests e.e_i again.
architectural_contract.valid_response_route: An accepted input returns (e, true); the iterator increments i exactly once and invokes next(e), causing State_(i+1) to construct its state object. Function_i does not call State_(i+1).
architectural_contract.functional_argument_passing: The context e is the explicit argument to Function_i, next(e) and State_i. Pending diagnostics travel in e.error. No second state argument or implicit global state is used to convey validation results.
architectural_contract.startup_defaults: The iterator initializes i=0, e={} unless resuming a saved run, then calls next(e). State_0 may define a default e={} for direct initial invocation; retries are always handled through the iterator retaining the index.
architectural_contract.deferred_or_immediate_invocation: The selected behavior is neither a direct handler call to a destination state nor a deferred state-pointer return. A handler returns only (e, valid). The iterator alone updates the index and invokes the current state via next(e).

mandatory_behavior.deterministic_selection: Preserve the State × Event lookup at Dispatch[State_i][E_RETURN] and use the selected Function_i to determine the validation Boolean; do not encode acceptance in event type or delegate acceptance to the agent.
mandatory_behavior.schema_validation_and_retry: Validate e.e_i with the current state's schema and semantic constraints. On failure, set e.error and return (e,false), resulting in a same-index error-mode retry; on success return (e,true), resulting in advancement by one.
mandatory_behavior.separate_context_and_state_argument: The complete context e alone carries accepted inputs and the optional e.error diagnostic to the state; no destination-specific second state argument is required under the iterator contract.
mandatory_behavior.no_global_state_dependency: Pass all ordinary inter-operation context explicitly through e. The iterator index belongs to persisted procedure-position data, not an inferred or agent-selected next state. Do not rely on hidden globals to move accepted inputs or errors.
mandatory_behavior.initial_state_defaults: State_0 may default its e parameter to {}, while next(e) supplies the same context explicitly on every normal start, retry, or continuation.

examples.title: Function_0 returns validation result without calling a state
examples.explanation: The dispatcher chooses Function_0 for State_0 × E_RETURN. The validation function returns e and a Boolean; the iterator handles progression.

examples.title: Iterator applies Boolean and renders the next state
examples.explanation: Both valid and invalid agent returns remain E_RETURN. The iterator advances only for a true Boolean; a false Boolean repeats the same state with e.error.

examples.title: State captures an error before clearing
examples.explanation: Error mode adds the error diagnostic before the unchanged normal instruction and schema; externally configured content is rendered separately.

conformance: Conformance requires a dedicated Function_i selected by State_i × E_RETURN, zero-based e.e_i validation, return of (e,valid), pending e.error on failure, iterator-controlled i advancement or retention, and no direct state invocation by the validator.

title: Agent Event Representation and Context Property Accumulation
applicability: Applies to agent response events and the named input properties in the context/event object e during the interactive State × Event procedure.

requirements.title: Event representation
requirements.required_behavior: Represent an agent's submitted response as the event E_RETURN(e), where E_RETURN identifies the occurrence of the agent returning its response and e is the complete context/event object containing the response values. Event presentation must preserve the distinction between the event occurrence and the object carried by that event.

requirements.title: Unique input addresses
requirements.required_behavior: Assign each independently recallable input its own address. In the indexed prototype, State_0 requests e.e0 for the verbatim prompt, State_1 requests e.e1 for intent, and each State_i requests e.e_i; these accepted addresses remain stable in later context.

requirements.title: Context accumulation
requirements.required_behavior: When e.e_i is accepted, preserve earlier accepted properties e.e0 through e.e_(i-1) and append or update the accepted value at e.e_i. e.error is a transient validation diagnostic consumed during the next state construction, not a replacement for an accepted input.

requirements.title: Property ownership
requirements.required_behavior: For each State_i document exactly what the agent must supply at e.e_i and its shape in the externally referenced instruction and JSON schema. Function_i, selected by Dispatch[State_i][E_RETURN], validates that property and returns (e,valid) to the iterator.

example.title: Indexed event and accumulated independent input addresses
sequence: State_0 requests e.e0; the agent returns E_RETURN(e) with e.e0 populated.
Function_0 accepts e.e0 and the iterator advances to State_1, which requests intent at e.e1.
The agent returns E_RETURN(e) with preserved e.e0 and newly populated e.e1.
Function_1 validates e.e1 and returns (e, valid) without selecting or invoking a state.

title: File-Level Change Mapping as the Procedure's Structural Foundation
applicability: The procedure-design phase that compares the current system state with the user-requested desired final system state, identifies filesystem changes, identifies agent actions, maps the actions to those changes, and subsequently expands the mappings into a procedure.
purpose: Ensure that the procedure specifies concrete, individually identifiable file changes and the agent actions that produce each change, rather than producing an abstract action list disconnected from the desired final state.

required_behavior.file_level_granularity: For each filesystem transformation required by the desired final system state, describe the change at the level of the specific file affected. Give each separately identifiable file change its own change identifier, specify the affected file path, and classify its operation as create, modify, or delete. Do not substitute a broad directory-level or project-level description when a specific file change can be identified.
required_behavior.desired_state_traceability: Identify which required condition or conditions of the desired final system state each file-level change is intended to satisfy. Preserve these relationships using the existing identifiers assigned to the final-state requirements and changes.
required_behavior.actions_per_change: For each defined file change, identify the exact agent action or actions needed to produce that change. Map the action identifiers to the corresponding file-change identifier so the procedure can independently recover which actions effect which file changes. An action may be referenced by multiple change mappings where it produces multiple independently identified file changes.
required_behavior.mapping_as_skeleton: Treat the existing change-to-action mappings as the canonical skeleton of the procedure. When generating ordered steps, command examples, code examples, simulation outputs, execution observations, or diagnostics, extend or decorate those mappings without replacing them with an unrelated action list, dropping original identifiers, or losing the link to the desired final state.
required_behavior.completion_coverage: Represent every required file-level change in the mapping and associate it with its necessary actions. Where a required file change or action remains unmapped, identify the gap rather than silently omitting the requirement.

example.scenario: The user's desired final state requires adding a new JSON configuration file and modifying an existing JavaScript program to read it.

actions.description: Write the required configuration data to config/settings.json.
Modify src/app.js so it reads config/settings.json and uses the configured values.

example.interpretation: The two file changes remain separately addressable and traceable to the desired final-state conditions. Subsequent procedure and simulation stages add execution details to these same mappings rather than replacing them.

title: Two-Phase Interactive MCP Procedure Queue and Agent Handoff
applicability: The application workflow that uses the two-dimensional State × Event machine to develop a procedure with an initial agent, place the resulting procedure into a queue, and continue interactively with a second agent for review, execution, and post-execution diagnostics.
purpose: Establish that both sides of the queued handoff are interactive procedures, not an issue-comment job processor or an offline batch execution, so future queue design and implementation preserve the intended agent-facing MCP interaction.

required_behavior.first_phase_interactive_procedure: The first agent follows successive iterator-rendered State_i instructions from i=0, returning e.e_i as requested. The 2D dispatcher selects Function_i for E_RETURN; the iterator advances on true or retries the same state on false. The agent identifies required changes, maps them to actions, builds a procedure and simulates its commands, code and predicted effects.
required_behavior.queue_handoff: After the procedure-preparation phase reaches its defined handoff, the application places that prepared procedure and its accumulated context e into the queue for a second agent. The handoff must preserve the existing file-change identifiers, action identifiers, mapping relationships, return data, and other information required for continuation; the second agent must not have to reconstruct the procedure independently from a summary.
required_behavior.second_phase_interactive_procedure: The second agent receives the queued procedure and continues through its own interactive State × Event exchanges. That phase comprises reviewing the prepared procedure, executing the associated actions, and completing the post-execution diagnostic against the existing desired-state requirements and checklist. The second agent's interactive responses remain subject to state-specific machine-dialect instructions, JSON return schemas, and function-selected transitions.
required_behavior.mcp_based_queue: Expose the queue and both interactive procedure phases through the application's MCP-based interface. Treat IssueStack's issue-backed queue only as historical design context, not as a required implementation or an execution dependency; an Issue-comment-triggered workflow is not a substitute for the intended interactive MCP queue.
required_behavior.preserve_machine_architecture: Queue transport, assignment, suspension, resumption and phase transfer preserve the two State × Event dispatch dimensions, the zero-based iterator index, the accumulated context e, the schema-governed agent-return event, and the Boolean validation function that controls iterator advancement. The queue does not invent an alternate state-transition system.
required_behavior.retain_full_run: Ensure the application's complete run record encompasses both interactive phases, the queue handoff, actual execution results, and post-execution diagnostics. The queue must preserve continuity of the same procedure rather than treating the second phase as a new unrelated request.

example.title: Interactive procedure authoring followed by interactive review and execution
sequence: Agent 1 responds to the MCP-rendered State_0 request at e.e0 and the subsequent State_i requests at e.e_i, with each agent return validated by the dedicated Function_i selected by State_i × E_RETURN.
Agent 1 produces a file-level change-to-action mapping and decorates that mapping with the stepwise procedure and a proposed simulation containing commands, code and predicted effects.
The application queues that prepared procedure together with its existing context e and the information needed to continue its run.

Agent 2 receives the queued work with its saved index and context, reviews the proposed procedure through the same iterator-controlled State × Event exchanges, and preserves the complete accumulated run.
Agent 2 executes the reviewed procedure and interactively supplies actual execution observations and the decorated post-execution diagnostic checklist.
The application retains the complete record spanning both agents and the handoff.

implementation_boundary: This instruction specifies required queue behavior and relationships, not a queue storage format, claim protocol, scheduling policy, MCP tool naming convention, or specific implementation strategy. Those decisions must be made separately without changing the stated interactive two-phase behavior.

title: Runner, State-Event Dispatcher, State-Object Renderer, and Two Interactive Applications
applicability: Architecture of the MCP-based procedure system, including starting a procedure, resolving State × Event transitions, presenting state instructions, creating queued procedures, reviewing and executing queued jobs, post-execution review, and access to completed jobs.

runner.purpose: Coordinate the program lifecycle and the indexed iterator. The iterator, not a transition handler or renderer, is the sole controller of progression and retry, while the State × Event dispatcher remains the mechanism selecting the validation function.
runner.required_behavior: Initialize or restore the zero-based iterator index and e, invoke next(e), and render the state object. When E_RETURN(e) arrives, dispatch by current State_i and event type to Function_i, receive (e,valid), update i by Number(valid), and invoke next(e) again. Do not directly route to a state from within a validation handler.
runner.expected_interface: Coordinate initial and resumed execution, passing index i and context e to the iterator and (State_i,E_RETURN,e) to the separate dispatcher. A rendered state waits for the next agent return; no synchronous waiting within next(e) is implied.

state_event_dispatcher.purpose: Provide a separate function or script that resolves the intersection of the current state and event in the two-dimensional function-pointer table.
state_event_dispatcher.required_behavior: Look up the dedicated function pointer at Dispatch[State_i][E_RETURN] and invoke Function_i(e). The dispatcher does not alter i, render text, validate content itself, or choose a destination state.
state_event_dispatcher.expected_interface: Accept current State_i, event type and e and return the validation function's (e,valid) result to the iterator for Boolean-controlled progression.

state_object_construction.purpose: Keep state-specific instructional content separate from tool-response rendering.
state_object_construction.required_behavior: State_i(e) first checks e.error, snapshots pending diagnostic data, selects error or normal mode, clears e.error, and returns a state object containing external instruction, schema and optional error-presentation references with the context required for rendering. It does not render or change i.
state_object_construction.expected_interface: Receive the complete e from next(e); return a state object with state ID, mode, external content references and runtime data, including an error snapshot when one existed. No transition-handler-supplied second argument is required.

renderer.purpose: Use a separate rendering function or script to transform a state object into the agent-facing tool response.
renderer.required_behavior: Resolve all external content references from the state object. In error mode, conspicuously display the diagnostic before the full unchanged normal state instruction and JSON schema. In normal mode, display the instruction and schema. Never decide validation or transitions or hardcode system-authored text.
renderer.expected_interface: Accept a state object containing content references and runtime values; load the referenced configuration values from files external to executable scripts and return or emit the rendered tool response. The exact configuration format, file paths, rendering format, and implementation language are undecided.

applications.minimum_separation: Implement at least two distinct applications using the shared procedure architecture. They must not be collapsed into a single indistinguishable workflow that obscures the two interactive queue phases.

procedure_creation_application.purpose: Provide the interactive application through which an agent creates a procedure to satisfy a user request.
procedure_creation_application.required_behavior: Present successive state instructions through the runner and renderer, collect agent return-schema responses, derive file-level changes and mapped agent actions, and develop and simulate the procedure. At the defined handoff it must make the prepared procedure available as a queued job, preserving its context and mappings.

job_review_execution_application.purpose: Provide the interactive application through which an agent accesses queued jobs, inspects their prepared procedures, carries out their actions, performs post-execution review, and accesses completed jobs.
job_review_execution_application.required_behavior: Display available queued jobs and permit selecting a job for interactive review and execution through state responses. Present the prepared procedure and retained context, run its execution phase, and conduct the post-procedure diagnostic. Mark the job complete according to the defined completion condition after post-execution review, and support listing and displaying completed jobs and their recorded results.

responsibility_boundaries.responsibility: Coordinate procedure startup, agent return handling, iterator and dispatcher calls, persistence and interactive application lifecycle.
Maintain zero-based i, call State_i(e) through next(e), apply i+=Number(valid), and render the selected state.
Resolve Dispatch[State_i][E_RETURN] to the dedicated Function_i and invoke it with e.
Validate e.e_i, set e.error on rejection, return (e,valid); never invoke a destination state or modify i.
Capture and clear pending e.error, select normal or additive error mode, and return referenced state-object content.
Resolve referenced templates and schema; display error diagnostic before unchanged normal instruction when error mode is selected.
Display queued and completed jobs and interactively review, execute, diagnose and complete jobs.

illustrative_flow: The procedure-creation application initializes or restores iterator index i and context e. A new procedure begins with i=0 and e={}.

The iterator calls next(e); next invokes State_i(e). State_i checks e.error, captures any pending diagnostic, selects the rendering mode, clears the pending error marker, and returns a state object referencing external instruction, return-schema and optional diagnostic content.
The renderer resolves the state object's references and displays either the normal instruction and schema or a conspicuous diagnostic followed by that same complete normal instruction and schema.
The agent later returns E_RETURN(e). The dispatcher uses State_i and E_RETURN to select Function_i, which validates e.e_i and returns (e,valid), populating e.error on rejection.
The iterator sets i to i+Number(valid). A false result repeats the same state with additive error rendering; a true result advances exactly one state. It then invokes next(e).
The creation application queues its prepared procedure along with the accepted context, index, history and mappings so a second agent can resume without reconstructing the work.

The review/execution application uses the same iterator and State × Event dispatch behavior, records execution and post-execution diagnostics, and makes completed jobs available after defined completion conditions are satisfied.
unresolved_implementation_decisions: Do not infer a concrete programming language, module and script names, process topology, job-list presentation format, queue storage structure, job ownership policy, persistence serialization, or job-completion status protocol from this architectural entry. These details remain to be specified. This entry fixes component responsibilities and the minimum application separation without selecting those implementation details.

title: External Addressable Content and Reference-Only Rendering
applicability: Every script, module, state function, transition function, runner, dispatcher, renderer, and interactive application that creates or displays agent-facing tool responses or other system-generated interface text in this workspace.
purpose: Separate all rendered wording and configurable display content from executable scripts. Every displayed instruction, prompt, label, diagnostic, explanatory sentence, or other system-authored text must be stored in independently addressable configuration resources rather than hardcoded in program source.

definitions.rendered_text: Any system-authored text that a program causes the agent or job viewer to see, including state instructions, return-schema explanations, validation errors, display headings, labels, queue/job prompts and completion diagnostics. Dynamically echoed agent inputs or observed command output are runtime data, not hardcoded display templates.
definitions.external_content_resource: A configuration file outside the executable script that stores content entries under stable addresses or keys. The exact file paths, format, and organization are not specified by this requirement.
definitions.content_reference: A stable, resolvable identifier recorded in a state object or other rendering input that selects a content entry from an external resource. A content reference is an address, not embedded display text.
definitions.rendering_resolution: The renderer loads the externally configured content selected by the references, incorporates explicitly supplied runtime values where needed, and produces the displayed response without composing system-authored wording in code.

mandatory_behavior.absolute_prohibition_on_embedded_render_: Do not hardcode, declare, concatenate, interpolate, or store any system-authored rendered text directly inside an executable script. A script may contain identifiers, references, control flow, field names, and runtime data operations; it must not carry the user-facing wording that those identifiers select.
mandatory_behavior.external_configurable_storage: Store every system-authored rendered text value in an addressable, configurable file located outside the executable script. Each value must have a uniquely specified reference that the application can resolve when needed. Updating display wording must be possible through the configuration resource without editing executable script source.
mandatory_behavior.reference_only_state_objects: State_i(e) returns references to externally stored normal instruction and JSON schema, and when e.error indicates a pending failure, also supplies a reference to diagnostic presentation plus a copied diagnostic payload. It must capture the error before clearing it and never embed actual rendered wording in executable code.
mandatory_behavior.reference_only_diagnostics: On failed validation Function_i records e.error with error=true, an errortype that identifies externally addressable diagnostic content, and any structured data needed for substitution. State_i snapshots the error into its state object and clears the indicator. The renderer resolves the diagnostic reference; no rendered error sentence may be hardcoded in a script.
mandatory_behavior.renderer_resolves_references: The separate renderer resolves the normal instruction and schema in every mode. In additive error mode it additionally resolves the diagnostic reference and displays it conspicuously before the unchanged normal content. Missing content references are program errors; the renderer must not invent fallback sentences.
mandatory_behavior.all_applications_in_scope: Apply the same reference-only rendering rule to both the interactive procedure-creation application and the queued-job review/execution/completion application. This includes job lists, job selection, completed-job displays and post-execution review wording.
mandatory_behavior.external_schema_content: Where JSON return schemas or their explanatory text are displayed, store the displayed schema definitions and any explanatory copy in externally addressable configuration resources. State scripts identify the applicable schema by reference rather than embedding complete schema definitions in source.
mandatory_behavior.preserve_machine_dialect: Externally stored state instructions must still satisfy the machine-dialect writing rules, describe every non-trivial schema key in sentence form, and align with the referenced valid JSON return schema. Moving content into configuration does not relax the state-input contract.

example.title: State snapshots pending diagnostic and renderer resolves external content
example.interpretation: Only identifiers and control logic are in script. In error mode the externally supplied formatResponse configuration shows the resolved diagnostic before the full unchanged normal instruction and schema. The diagnostic remains available after e.error is cleared because the state captured it in the returned object.

implementation_boundary: This entry requires reference-only configuration-driven rendering but does not decide which configuration file format, directory, resource loader, caching method, template engine or renderer implementation to use. Those decisions are separate from the non-negotiable prohibition on hardcoded rendered text.

title: Dedicated Dispatch-Cell Validation Functions and Iterator-Controlled State Invocation
applicability: Each populated State × Event dispatch cell, its dedicated Function_i, validation outcomes, error production and iterator-controlled State_i invocation in the two interactive procedure applications.
architecture_decision: Retain one independently identifiable validation function pointer for every populated State × Event cell. For the prototype Dispatch[State_i][E_RETURN] = Function_i with i starting at zero. Function_i validates e.e_i and returns (e,valid); it never directly calls an earlier or following state. The iterator, not the function, controls index advancement or same-state retry.

mandatory_behavior.dedicated_handler_per_cell: Provide a separately identifiable Function_i for each populated (State_i,E_RETURN) intersection, validating the e.e_i input requested by that state. Never replace the function-pointer table with a monolithic conditional dispatcher.
mandatory_behavior.invalid_input: On schema or semantic validation failure, Function_i populates e.error with error=true, an errortype identifying externally configured diagnostic presentation, and any structured supporting data; it returns (e,false). The iterator retains i and calls next(e).
mandatory_behavior.accepted_input: On successful validation, Function_i returns (e,true); the iterator increments i by exactly one and calls next(e). The handler does not select or invoke State_(i+1).
mandatory_behavior.state_builds_not_renders: The iterator invokes State_i(e). The state captures e.error when present, selects an additive error-mode or normal-mode object, clears e.error, and returns external references and runtime data. It never renders.
mandatory_behavior.renderer_outputs_state_object: The renderer displays resolved error material conspicuously before the full unchanged normal instruction and JSON schema when mode is error. It does not validate, change i, or choose a function pointer.
mandatory_behavior.preserve_reference_only_text: All displayed state instructions, error messages, schema content, labels and formatting are externally configured and addressed by reference. Function and state identifiers used for program control are not rendered instruction strings.
mandatory_behavior.procedure_specific_behavior: Validation functions contain only the validation and diagnostic logic applicable to their specific dispatch cells. Their Boolean drives the iterator's only index branch, and no additional transition mechanisms are introduced without separate procedural specification.

illustrative_example.purpose: At State_2 × E_RETURN, Function_2 validates e.e2, returning (e,false) with e.error on rejection or (e,true) on acceptance; the iterator renders State_2 again or advances to State_3.
illustrative_example.interpretation: The handler has no arbitrary state switch and does not invoke a state. The iterator changes only the index and invokes next(e). A rejected return is still E_RETURN(e), and the rendered diagnostic is resolved from external content.

implementation_selection: The zero-based indexed iterator with Boolean-controlled state advancement replaces the former direct preceding/following state invocation design. Historical direct-call examples elsewhere are superseded and must be reconciled rather than treated as active alternatives.

title: Indexed Procedure Iterator, Boolean Validation Branching, and Additive Error-Mode Rendering
applicability: Every initialization, state invocation, agent-return event, validation operation, index transition, retry, state rendering, and procedure continuation governed by the indexed State × Event function-pointer machine in this workspace.
purpose: Define a deterministic iterator that invokes state functions in index order, uses the Boolean result of the state-event-selected validation function to advance or repeat the current state, and communicates validation failures through a single-use error property in the accumulated context object e.

definitions.iterator_index: The nonnegative integer i identifies the current procedure position. The initial index is zero. State_i and Function_i correspond to the same index i.
definitions.context_object: The object e carries previously accepted agent inputs, the current agent response, and any pending validation diagnostic. The context is passed explicitly between procedural operations.
definitions.state_function: State_i(e) constructs and returns the state object corresponding to procedure index i. It checks for a pending validation error before selecting its rendering mode.
definitions.validation_function: Function_i(e) validates the agent response at e.e_i against the schema and semantic constraints issued by State_i. It returns the context object and a Boolean validation result.
definitions.validation_boolean: The Boolean returned by Function_i is true when the requested input is accepted and false when rejected. This Boolean is determined by application validation rather than by the agent.
definitions.error_property: The property e.error is reserved for validation diagnostics. A populated error object identifies a failed validation and supplies error type and diagnostic information required for rendering.
definitions.normal_mode: The rendering mode that displays the complete ordinary instruction and JSON return schema associated with the current state.
definitions.error_mode: The rendering mode that conspicuously displays the pending validation diagnostic before the complete, unchanged normal instruction and JSON return schema for the same state.

mandatory_behavior.initialization: Initialize iterator index i=0 and e={} unless an existing procedure context and index have explicitly been supplied for continuation. Invoke next(e) to render the initial state.
mandatory_behavior.state_invocation: When next(e) executes, invoke State_i(e) at the current index. The state function receives the full context and constructs a state object with external content references and runtime data for the separate renderer.
mandatory_behavior.error_detection: At the beginning of State_i(e), inspect e.error. A populated validation error object with error=true selects error mode; an absent, null or cleared marker selects normal mode.
mandatory_behavior.error_snapshot_and_reset: When a pending validation error exists, preserve its diagnostic data in the returned state object before clearing e.error. Use null or false as the final cleared representation according to the implementation's selected error-value contract. Resetting does not change the index or previously accepted context.
mandatory_behavior.normal_rendering: In normal mode, construct a state object referencing the complete machine-dialect instruction and JSON return schema for State_i. The renderer resolves these from externally configured resources.
mandatory_behavior.error_rendering: In error mode, construct a state object referencing the same unchanged normal instruction and JSON return schema plus an additional conspicuous error presentation before them. Do not replace, abbreviate or modify the normal instruction or schema.
mandatory_behavior.agent_response: After rendering the state object, receive the agent's later response as E_RETURN(e). Its event type must not encode validity. The response carries the complete context and the input e.e_i requested by the current state's schema.
mandatory_behavior.function_selection: Select Function_i from Dispatch[State_i][E_RETURN]. State and event type remain the two dispatch dimensions; the index identifies the current state but does not replace the table.
mandatory_behavior.input_validation: Function_i independently validates e.e_i against the referenced JSON return schema and applicable semantic constraints, not against an agent-generated pass/fail judgment.
mandatory_behavior.validation_success: When the current input is accepted, Function_i returns the complete accepted e and Boolean true. The iterator increments i exactly once and invokes next(e).
mandatory_behavior.validation_failure: When the current input fails validation, Function_i populates e.error with an object having error=true and errortype identifying the validation failure, supplemented by externally configured diagnostic references and structured facts as required. It returns (e,false).
mandatory_behavior.index_retention: When Function_i returns false, retain i and invoke next(e). The same State_i captures the pending diagnostic, clears e.error and constructs an error-mode state object requesting corrected e.e_i.
mandatory_behavior.boolean_transition: Compute i_next=i+Number(valid), with true contributing 1 and false contributing 0. Neither agent input nor renderer may independently advance the index.
mandatory_behavior.recursive_continuation: After a validation result and index update, invoke next(e). Each call constructs and renders exactly the state at the current index, preparing the next agent interaction.
mandatory_behavior.interaction_boundary: Rendering a state and receiving the agent's subsequent response are distinct interaction phases. Do not assume the response is synchronously available inside next(e); continuation occurs when the agent submits E_RETURN(e).
mandatory_behavior.context_preservation: Preserve accepted properties at their original e.e_i addresses. Failed validation must not erase earlier accepted inputs. e.error is transient and must not become a new dispatch event type.
mandatory_behavior.function_responsibility_boundary: Function_i validates the current input, records diagnostic context on failure, and returns (e,valid). It must not directly invoke State_i, State_(i+1), render, or change the index.
mandatory_behavior.renderer_responsibility_boundary: The renderer resolves externally configured templates and schemas and produces output. It does not validate returns, select transition functions, change i, or independently determine error state.
mandatory_behavior.persistence_and_handoff: Preserve the current iterator index, accepted context, pending diagnostic and run identity when suspending, queuing or resuming. Continue at the saved procedure position without constructing an unrelated run.
mandatory_behavior.non_deviation: Do not substitute direct destination-state calls, agent-chosen routing, validity-coded event types or monolithic conditional dispatch for Boolean-controlled index advancement. Preserve dedicated pointers at State × Event intersections.

interface_contracts.iterator_entry: next(e) invokes the state function identified by current i and sends its state object to the renderer.
interface_contracts.validation_return: Function_i(e) returns the complete context object and one Boolean validity value.

failure_error_shape.errortype: An identifier for an applicable externally configured validation diagnostic, with structured data as needed.

interface_contracts.continuation: After the index update, invoke next(e) with the context returned by Function_i.

execution_examples.title: Initial successful validation
sequence: Initialize i=0 and e={}.
next(e) invokes State_0(e), which returns a normal-mode state object; the renderer requests e.e0 using the normal instruction and JSON schema.
The agent returns E_RETURN(e) containing e.e0.
Dispatch[State_0][E_RETURN] selects Function_0, which accepts e.e0 and returns (e,true).
The iterator increments i from zero to one and invokes next(e), producing State_1 normal mode.

execution_examples.title: Failed validation and same-state retry
sequence: At i=2 the agent returns invalid e.e2 after the State_2 instruction.
Dispatch[State_2][E_RETURN] selects Function_2, which sets e.error with error=true and errortype, returning (e,false).
The iterator retains i=2 and calls next(e).
State_2 captures e.error into its state object, selects error mode, and clears the error marker.
The renderer conspicuously displays the diagnostic followed by the full unchanged normal instruction and JSON schema for State_2.

execution_examples.title: Successful correction after retry
sequence: The agent returns corrected e.e2 in another E_RETURN(e).
Function_2 validates and returns (e,true); the iterator increments i from 2 to 3.
next(e) invokes State_3 normally, preserving e.e0, e.e1 and accepted e.e2.

relationship_to_existing_workspace_instr.preserved_requirements: Preserve the State × Event dispatch table, dedicated validation functions, external rendering resources, full context accumulation, machine-dialect instructions, aligned JSON return schemas, persistent run records and interactive two-phase queue design.
relationship_to_existing_workspace_instr.superseded_transition_behavior: Replace requirements that Function_i directly invoke preceding/following state functions. Function_i instead returns (e,valid), and the iterator selects the current state by index.
relationship_to_existing_workspace_instr.superseded_index_convention: Use zero-based correspondence between State_i, Function_i, and e.e_i. Earlier examples with State_0/Function_1/e.e1 do not define the active indexing convention.
relationship_to_existing_workspace_instr.reconciliation_requirement: Maintain one authoritative iterator and transition mechanism across all current instruction objects and implementation examples; do not leave competing active direct-invocation contracts.

title: State Object Composition and Context-Derived Return Schemas
applicability: Every State_i(e) function in the indexed State × Event procedure machine when constructing the JSON state object that will be presented through the renderer, including normal and validation-error responses.
purpose: Specify the mandatory and conditional content members of a state object and permit a state-local helper function to derive its return schema from one or more independently addressable properties of the accumulated context e without hardcoding rendered content.

definitions.state_object: The JSON object constructed and returned by State_i(e) for the current state. It contains two mandatory content members, instruction and return_schema, and may contain one additional content member, error_message, when a validation diagnostic is pending.
definitions.instruction: The mandatory content member describing the current state's agent-facing instruction. Its system-authored wording is obtained through the externally configured content mechanism; it must not be hardcoded into the state function.
definitions.return_schema: The mandatory content member specifying the syntactically valid JSON return schema governing the input requested from the agent by the current state. The schema can be obtained from an external configured resource or derived at runtime by the state's schema helper using declared inputs from e.
definitions.error_message: The conditional content member containing or referencing the diagnostic for a pending validation failure. It accompanies, rather than replaces, the mandatory instruction and return_schema members.
definitions.state_local_schema_helper: An optional function defined within State_i that receives one or more specified properties of e and computes the current state's return schema from their accepted values. Its output is used as the return_schema component of the constructed state object.

mandatory_behavior.mandatory_components: State_i(e) must construct a JSON state object containing both instruction and return_schema on every invocation, whether or not a validation error exists. Neither component may be omitted, substituted by error_message, or replaced with a mere statement that the component will be produced later.
mandatory_behavior.conditional_error_component: Include error_message when e.error indicates a pending validation error. Capture the diagnostic needed for error presentation before clearing e.error according to the existing iterator rule. When no validation error exists, omit the error_message content member.
mandatory_behavior.normal_and_error_composition: A normal response includes instruction and return_schema. An error response includes error_message in addition to the same complete normal instruction and return_schema; the error message is displayed conspicuously before the normal instruction by the existing rendering mechanism.
mandatory_behavior.instruction_content_source: The instruction member must identify or carry the state-specific instruction obtained from externally addressable configuration content. Constructing the JSON state object does not authorize hardcoding any system-authored instruction wording in executable source.
mandatory_behavior.schema_source_selection: For each state invocation, supply a return_schema from either an externally configured schema definition or a dynamically constructed schema. Dynamic construction must produce a concrete, syntactically valid JSON Schema for the input requested at the current State_i, not an unexplained placeholder or abbreviated pseudo-schema.
mandatory_behavior.optional_state_local_helper: A State_i function may define a dedicated schema-construction helper inside its own function body. When used, the helper must receive one or more explicitly identified properties of e as inputs and derive the return_schema from their values. The helper is optional; the requirement does not force dynamic construction where an externally configured schema suffices.
mandatory_behavior.context_derivation: The helper must use the declared input values in e to determine the applicable fields, types and constraints of the return schema. Its logic must preserve the semantics of previously accepted context properties and must not alter those properties merely to construct a schema.
mandatory_behavior.schema_instruction_alignment: Whether loaded or derived, return_schema must describe the same expected agent response as instruction, including the newly requested e.e_i and any required previously accepted context values. The schema used to validate the subsequent agent return must correspond to the schema presented for that state interaction.
mandatory_behavior.separate_rendering_responsibility: State_i constructs and returns the JSON state object; the separate renderer presents its components to the agent. The state function's object construction is not permission to hardcode rendered prose, render the MCP tool response itself, validate the agent's later return, or advance the iterator index.
mandatory_behavior.preserve_existing_architecture: This entry governs state-object composition and schema derivation only. It does not replace the State × Event dispatch table, Boolean validation branching, error-clearing procedure, reference-only restriction on hardcoded rendered text, or the existing iterator progression contract.

composition_examples.title: Normal state object

content_members.instruction: Reference or resolved value of the externally configured state instruction

composition_examples.interpretation: The instruction and JSON return schema are present; error_message is omitted because no validation error is pending. The schema is illustrative content, not an instruction to hardcode it into executable source.

composition_examples.title: Error-mode state object

content_members.instruction: Reference or resolved value of the same externally configured state instruction
content_members.error_message: Reference or resolved diagnostic captured from e.error

composition_examples.interpretation: The pending diagnostic is additional to the two mandatory components. The renderer places the diagnostic conspicuously before the unchanged normal instruction and schema.

composition_examples.title: State-local helper deriving a schema from context
composition_examples.interpretation: This is illustrative control logic: the helper receives accepted questions at e.e2 and derives a state-specific JSON Schema without embedding a fixed rendered schema or instruction. Referenced instruction and diagnostic wording remain in external resources. The concrete helper implementation and naming are not prescribed.

conformance: A state object conforms when it always contains instruction and a valid return_schema; includes error_message only when a pending diagnostic exists; preserves the full normal instruction and schema in error mode; and uses external content references or runtime derivation rather than hardcoding rendered instruction, diagnostic, or fixed schema content in executable code.
